answer: Each orchard identity posts a 70-credit bond for a pest-trap row on a glacier channel. Its pearl tag binds trap, row, and epoch key, and it files catches with the flow reading. Auditors check the pearl tag and recompute catch-per-flow from the board; a reused tag, copied flow reading, or mismatched catch burns the bond. The first line costs 29 credits, the k-th 29+8(k-1), so the 1000th costs 8021 and 1000 fakes pay 4,025,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-trap ring fails: one trap cannot yield catches for two rows. An honest grower pays 29 once, recovering the bond after a clean audit.
